cap_source: driver level_cap from the ROM (dossier prose still says 'cap 76' and is stale)
availability_note: Routes 132-134 are sailed after Mossdeep with Dive earned, Sootopolis not entered. Party uses only gate<=68 pool-84 entries (Incineroar 36, Urshifu-S 42, Amoonguss 42, Landorus 42, Tapu Fini 60, Flutter Mane 68); no gate-84 Underwater/Seafloor species. Landorus and Tapu Fini are reachable legends per the brief and are noted as such.

strategy_checks.check: Aerodactyl selects Tailwind in the first two turns
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 Aerodactyl chose MOVE_TAILWIND (flinched by Fake Out); T2 it chose Tailwind again and it resolved - 'A tailwind started blowing on the opposing side!'

strategy_checks.check: Rampardos attacks under Sheer Force while the support sets up
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 Rampardos chose Rock Slide at battler 0; it was KOed by Close Combat before the move resolved, so no Sheer Force / Life Orb recoil-cancel damage was observed.

strategy_checks.check: Base Sableye uses Prankster support before the Mega transition
strategy_checks.evidence: T2 base Sableye used priority Fake Out on Urshifu (flinch denied my attack); T3 it Mega Evolved into Mega Sableye with Magic Bounce and from then on moved at normal speed (Will-O-Wisp resolved after Wicked Blow).

strategy_checks.check: Mega transition timed so Prankster is spent first, not wasted
strategy_checks.evidence: The AI held the Mega until after Fake Out was used, exactly the 'deliberate Mega transition' the plan describes.
T3 Will-O-Wisp burned Urshifu; the halved Attack is what let Mega Sableye survive the follow-up Wicked Blow and Recover.

strategy_checks.check: Sawsbuck's Sap Sipper / Clear Amulet matter
strategy_checks.evidence: I deliberately brought no Grass move and Clear Amulet blocked nothing because Incineroar's Intimidate had already fired before Sawsbuck entered.

strategy_checks.check: Mega Sableye uses Recover at a sensible threshold
strategy_checks.evidence: T4 at 101/290 it used Recover back to full while its partner Sawsbuck traded a KO.

protect_ledger.entry: No opponent used Protect in this battle. Rampardos, Aerodactyl and Sawsbuck each carry Protect and never selected it; the AI attacked or set Tailwind instead, which was correct every time because it was never facing a predictable lethal it could stall out.

level_changes.why: It never landed a hit: at offset 1 it is L83 with 280 HP and dies to one Intimidated Close Combat before the Tailwind it depends on is even up. The whole concept needs it to survive to turn 2.
Two Dark attacks removed it on turn 3 with its Focus Sash knocked off, one turn after the Tailwind landed. A durability step lets the speed window actually be spent.

level_changes_unverified: Level changes cannot be re-verified until the main agent rebuilds the headless ROM; the reported attempt was played at the pre-change offsets (Rampardos/Aerodactyl L83).
most_worth_rerunning: E0434 attempt at the new offsets - specifically whether Rampardos survives an Intimidated super-effective Fighting hit on turn 1, which is the single fact the whole Tailwind concept rests on.
cooler: The fight works and the base-Prankster-then-Mega sequencing is genuinely nice to watch the AI perform. The concept's real gap is that Tailwind arrives a turn after Rampardos is already dead, so the player never has to respect the speed window. Nothing here needs a species change; what it wants (not in this pass) is Rampardos holding something that buys the first turn - the dossier's own Focus Sash idea belongs on the glass cannon rather than on the setter that survives anyway.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem found. All four sets materialized and played as written; Mega Sableye correctly lost Prankster on evolving and its Sablenite correctly resisted Knock Off.
